eyebrow: Learn Fresh · NYC site visit 12 Oct + WestEd interviews 22 Oct 2026 · Documentary
title: The NBA Math Hoops RCT:
length: about 10 to 15 min (this plan maps the first assembly)
headline: For ten years people said math and basketball sounds fun, but does it work? The NBA Math Hoops RCT answers: yes, and fast.
story: The film is about the NBA Math Hoops RCT only. Arc: the assumption (fun, but rigorous?) → where the game came from → why an RCT and why Jackson, Mississippi → the result in plain words → the kids in the room → what schools need and what comes next.

It is the public launch of the findings and the centerpiece of Learn Fresh's “Make Every Hour Count” end-of-year giving push, so it closes on Donate. The Jackson school district interview is still being scheduled (target 20 Nov); its slot is held in chapter 2.

Loops: L1 “Fun, but does it work?” opens at 0:00 and closes in chapter 3. L2 “Why should schools care?” opens in chapter 2 and closes in chapter 5. Stakes: programs that are fun get taken less seriously.
do: Open on a kid, not on a logo or a title: hook text on frame 1.
Explain the RCT in plain words before any number.
Numbers as cards: 50th → 58th percentile, 12 to 14 days, 17 to 24 hours, four to five months, 2 hours of training.
Real NYC room sound between chapters.
Close on Dannyse's ask, then the Donate end card.
dont: Never say the result is true for other Learn Fresh programs.
NBA Math Hoops is a supplement to math class, never a replacement.
Do not criticise ed-tech or AI.
No school names on screen, no student last names, no logo before the end card.

chapters.title: Cold open
chapters.line: A kid says math used to be boring. The CEO names the assumption the film answers: fun, but rigorous?

chapters.title: Fun, but does it work?
chapters.line: Where NBA Math Hoops came from and why it is about math, not fandom. The room shows sports kids and math kids at one table.

chapters.title: The study
chapters.line: Why Learn Fresh needed an RCT, what makes an RCT the gold standard, and why Jackson, Mississippi.

chapters.title: The result
chapters.line: The numbers in plain words: 50th to 58th percentile in 12 to 14 days, four to five months of learning in 17 to 24 hours.

chapters.title: In the room
chapters.line: Kids in their own words: math with others, not alone; fast, social, fun.

chapters.title: What comes next
chapters.line: What schools need, the next study, and the message: rigor and joy together. Ends on the ask.

The end card says Donate to Learn Fresh and learnfresh.org.
